title: What Respiratory Therapists Do
description: Respiratory therapists care for patients with breathing disorders — from asthma and COPD to premature infants and ventilated ICU patients. They assess lung function, deliver oxygen and aerosol medications, manage ventilators, perform chest physiotherapy, and respond to codes. They are the airway experts of the hospital.
key_points: Asthma to ventilated ICU: full spectrum
how_it_works: Deliver prescribed oxygen and aerosol therapy
Monitor response and adjust per protocol
requirements: Associate or bachelor's degree in respiratory therapy (accredited program)
NBRC credentials: CRT then RRT (Registered Respiratory Therapist)
standards: Evidence-based oxygen titration, not routine high-flow
Ventilator management per lung-protective protocols
Accurate arterial blood gas interpretation
Infection control for all airway equipment
safety: Verify ventilator settings with two-person checks
Humidification and airway clearance to prevent mucus plugging
Monitor for barotrauma and oxygen toxicity
Emergency airway readiness at every bedside
troubleshooting: Desaturation: check airway, circuit, then ventilator
High airway pressures: suction, check tube position, assess compliance
Patient-ventilator asynchrony: adjust trigger, sedation per orders
Nebulizer not misting: check gas flow and medication cup
citations: American Association for Respiratory Care guidance; National Board for Respiratory Care standards; respiratory therapy clinical references.
provenance: Public trade knowledge drawn from respiratory therapy education, professional association guidance, and critical-care references. Real, fact-checked records.

title: A Day in the Life
description: Hospital RTs start with ventilator rounds — checking every vented patient — then work through breathing treatments, ABGs, and assessments ordered through the day. They attend high-risk deliveries, respond to rapid responses and codes, and hand off vent settings meticulously at shift change. Every breath counts, literally.

title: Safety in Respiratory Care

title: Oxygen Therapy Done Right
description: Oxygen is titrated to target saturations — typically 92-96% for most adults, 88-92% for COPD patients at risk of CO2 retention. Delivery scales with need: nasal cannula for mild hypoxemia, Venturi masks for precise FiO2, high-flow for work of breathing, noninvasive ventilation for failure. More is not better; right is better.

Choose the device for the need

title: History of Respiratory Therapy
description: The field grew from oxygen orderlies and iron-lung technicians of the polio era into a degreed profession. The 1940s-50s polio epidemics created the first positive-pressure ventilator expertise; the NBRC (1960) and AARC professionalized it. Each epidemic since — including COVID-19 — proved the RT's essential role.
